title: The wood wide web
text: A forest looks like a contest: tall trees crowd {{1}} another for light, and foresters have long counted trunks rather than connections. Underground the picture is different, because tree roots {{2}} linked by threads of fungus that pass water, nutrients and chemical warnings between neighbouring plants. The network carries {{3}} only food but also alarm signals, which a damaged tree can send to its neighbours. {{4}} oldest trees in a stand, nicknamed mother trees, appear to use the network to nurture the seedlings around them. Ecologists have called {{5}} the wood wide web, although not everyone is convinced; a number of researchers, {{6}} doubts centre on the early experiments, insist that {{7}} the fungi act as partners or as parasites remains an open question. Either way, the findings are already beginning to feed {{8}} conservation policy.

gaps.explanation: 'One another' is the reciprocal phrase used for more than two.
Present passive with a plural subject: roots are linked.

gaps.hint: negation: carries ___ only food but also
gaps.explanation: 'Not only … but also' is the fixed correlative pair.

gaps.hint: article: ___ oldest trees in a stand
gaps.explanation: Superlatives take the definite article: the oldest trees.

gaps.hint: pronoun: have called ___ the wood wide web
gaps.explanation: 'It' refers back to the network as the object of 'called'.

gaps.hint: conjunction: ___ the fungi act as partners or parasites
gaps.explanation: Fronted subject clause; 'whether … or' presents the two alternatives.
'Feed into' — the particle completes the phrasal verb meaning 'contribute to'.
